places.name: Thebes
names: Before the Palace of Oedipus at Thebes
places.description: the Boeotian city ruled by Oedipus, stricken by plague, setting of the whole play

wikipedia.lead: Thebes is a city in Boeotia, Central Greece, and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It is the largest city in Boeotia and a major center for the region.

places.name: Kithairon
places.description: mountain where the infant Oedipus was left to die and rescued by a shepherd

wikipedia.lead: Cithaeron or Kithairon is a mountain and mountain range about sixteen kilometres (ten miles) long in Central Greece. The range is the physical boundary between Boeotia region in the north and Attica region in the south.

places.name: Phokis
places.description: region containing the crossroads where Oedipus killed Laius

wikipedia.lead: Phocis is one of the regional units of Greece. It is part of the administrative region of Central Greece.

places.name: Corinth
places.description: city where Polybus rules and Oedipus was raised, which he fled to avoid the prophecy

wikipedia.lead: Corinth was a city-state (polis) on the Isthmus of Corinth, the narrow stretch of land that joins the Peloponnese peninsula to mainland Greece, roughly halfway between Athens and Sparta. The modern city of Corinth is located approximately 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) northeast of the ancient ruins.

places.name: Palace
places.description: the royal palace of Thebes, before which the play is set and where Oedipus and Creon appear

places.name: Delphi
places.description: Apollo's oracle sanctuary, where Creon and Oedipus sought prophecies

wikipedia.lead: Delphi, in legend previously called Pytho (Πυθώ), was an ancient sacred precinct in central Greece. It was the seat of Pythia, the major oracle who was consulted about important decisions throughout the ancient classical world.

places.name: Hell
places.description: the realm of the dead, Hades, mentioned in curses and laments

wikipedia.lead: Hades, in the ancient Greek religion and mythology, is the god of the dead and riches and the King of the underworld, with which his name became synonymous. Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

places.name: Olympus
places.description: home of the gods, mentioned in the chorus

wikipedia.lead: Mount Olympus is an extensive massif near the Thermaic Gulf of the Aegean Sea, in Greece, located on the border between Thessaly and Macedonia, between the regional units of Larissa and Pieria, about 80 km (50 mi) southwest from Thessaloniki. Mount Olympus has 52 peaks and deep gorges.

places.name: Abantes
places.description: Euboean land of the Abantes, named in the chorus

wikipedia.lead: Euboea, also known as Evia, is the second-largest Greek island in area and population, after Crete, and the sixth largest island in the Mediterranean Sea. It is separated from Boeotia in mainland Greece by the narrow Euripus Strait (only 40 m (130 ft) at its narrowest point), the North Euboean Gulf, and the South Euboean Gulf.

Mount Kyllini or Mount Cyllene, also known as Mount Ziria (Ζήρια, Modern Greek: [ˈzirja]), is a mountain on the Peloponnese in Greece famous for its association with the god Hermes. It rises to 2,376 m (7,795 ft) above sea level, making it the second highest point on the peninsula.

places.name: Daulia
places.description: town in Phokis on the road where the crossways lay

wikipedia.lead: Daulis, at a later time Daulia (Δαυλία), and also Daulium or Daulion (Δαύλιον), was a town of ancient Phocis, near the frontiers of Boeotia, and on the road from Orchomenus and Chaeroneia to Delphi.

places.name: Helicon
places.description: Boeotian mountain of the Muses, evoked in the chorus

wikipedia.lead: Mount Helicon is a mountain in the region of Thespiai in Boeotia, Greece, celebrated in Greek mythology. With an altitude of 1,749 metres (5,738 ft), it is located approximately 10 kilometres (6 mi) from the north coast of the Gulf of Corinth.

places.name: Ismenus
places.description: Theban river, whose prophetic ashes are mentioned

places.name: Ister
places.description: the Danube, named among rivers that cannot wash the house clean

wikipedia.lead: The Danube is a river in Europe, the second-longest after the Volga. It flows through Central and Southeastern Europe, from the Black Forest of Germany south through the Danube Delta in Romania into the Black Sea.

places.name: Olympia
places.description: sacred site in Elis, named in the chorus

wikipedia.lead: Olympia, officially Archaia Olympia (Greek: Αρχαία Ολυμπία lit. 'Ancient Olympia'), is a small town in Elis on the Peloponnese peninsula in Greece, famous for the nearby archaeological site of the same name. The site was a major Panhellenic religious sanctuary of ancient Greece, where the ancient Olympic Games were held every four years throughout classical antiquity, from the 8th century BC to the 4th century AD. They were restored on a global basis in 1894 in honor of the ideal of peaceful international contention for excellence.

places.name: Phasis
places.description: river of Colchis, named among great rivers

wikipedia.lead: The Rioni is the main river of western Georgia. It originates in the Caucasus Mountains, in the region of Racha and flows west to the Black Sea, entering it north of the city of Poti (near ancient Phasis).

places.name: Thrace
places.description: northeastern land, shore of the sea to which the war-god is asked to drive away

wikipedia.lead: Thrace (, thrayss) is a geographical and historical region in Southeast Europe roughly corresponding to the province of Thrace in the Roman Empire. Bounded by the Balkan Mountains to the north, the Aegean Sea to the south, and the Black Sea to the east, it comprises present-day southeastern Bulgaria, northeastern Greece, and the European part of Turkey, corresponding to Northern, Western and East Thrace respectively.
